title: Confocal Microscopy Imaging for Opaline Silica Single Cell Skeletons
author: Miguel Mendez Sandin
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.t5qeq5w

steps.title: Recover and store skeleton
steps.instruction: Recover the skeleton from the eluted pellet using a binocular or inverted microscope; dilute the extraction waste in milli‑Q water and store the skeletons at –20 °C until further processing.

steps.title: Initial rinsing of skeleton
steps.instruction: Rinse the skeleton several times with milli‑Q water to reduce residual SDS and other lysis reagents.

steps.title: Hydrogen peroxide treatment
steps.instruction: Treat the skeleton with hydrogen peroxide, heat, and then add water.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the skeleton into a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube containing 50 µL H₂O₂.
Heat the tube at 70 °C for 10 minutes to remove residual organic matter.

steps.title: Handpick and rinse skeleton
steps.instruction: Handpick the skeleton under a binocular or inverted microscope and rinse it several times with fresh milli‑Q water.

steps.title: Fluorescent staining of skeleton
steps.instruction: Stain the skeleton with fluorescent dye.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the skeleton into a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube containing 25 µL fluorescent staining mix (Colin et al., 2017).
Incubate the tube for 2 hours at room temperature in the dark.

steps.title: Dilute dye and final wash
steps.instruction: Dilute the dye and clean the skeleton.

substeps.instruction: Add 1.5 mL milli‑Q water to dilute the dye.
Handpick the skeleton and rinse several times with milli‑Q water to properly clean the sample.

steps.title: Transfer to micro‑well plate
steps.instruction: Transfer the cleaned skeleton into a micro‑well plate.

steps.title: Dry skeleton
steps.instruction: Dry the skeleton at 70 °C for 2 hours.
